channel.title: Block Club Chicago - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Block Club Chicago (blockclubchicago.org)

item.title: Ofelia Torres, Teen With Cancer Who Fought For Father’s Freedom From ICE, Has Died
item.description: Torres, 16, died Friday. Her father was arrested in October, the day after she returned from more than a month at the hospital for cancer treatments. She shared her family's plight, and her father was freed.

item.title: Chicago Could Set Record-High Temperature Monday As Warm Stretch Continues
item.description: Monday's forecast high of 64 degrees could set a record for highest temperature for Feb. 16. The warm stretch comes after one of the coldest periods in recent city history.

item.title: Teen Wanted In South Side Jewel Triple Shooting Arrested In Phoenix, Police Say
item.description: Elijah Theodore, 19, has been charged with attempted murder in a theft at the Jewel-Osco near 33rd Street and King Drive that ended in three people being shot, according to police.

item.title: A West Side Mailman Went Viral For Singing To A Widowed Grandmother. It Changed His Life
item.description: An Austin woman's doorbell camera caught Lavonte Harvey singing on his mail route, and she shared the video with her granddaughter. The viral video led neighbors to help Harvey buy a car.

item.title: Beef Tallow Has Been Big Business For This Bridgeport Company Since The ’70s
item.description: Animal fat is making headlines, but it’s old news to South Chicago Packing, a fifth-generation, family-owned business located near the former Union Stockyards.

item.title: Ancestry Moon Art Studio To Close In Beverly In March
item.description: After 10 years of classes, workshops and art therapy, the studio is closing because the building's new owners are not renewing tenants' leases, Ancestry Moon owner Salima Cobb-Collins said.

item.title: After Trump Denies August Flooding Disaster Aid, City Leaders Vow To ‘Get Creative’ To Help Neighbors
item.description: Following FEMA's decision to deny Illinois’ appeal for aid, alderpeople and community leaders are stepping up to help South and West side neighbors, from creating heat maps of flood-prone areas to reviewing sewer lines that need repairs.

item.title: Edgewater Apothecary Reopens On Broadway After Years Of Floods, Landlord Issues
item.description: Mother-and-son owners Deirdre Austin and Matthew Walcott moved DMApothecary out of a Sheridan Road building plagued by flooding and into a new location in Edgewater.

item.title: Amazon To Share Plans For Gage Park’s Central Steel & Wire Plant At Community Meeting
item.description: Amazon bought the 70-acre property in 2021 and plans to redevelop it into a delivery station. Neighbors can learn more at a Tuesday meeting at Las Brisas del Mar.

item.title: Chase No Longer Issuing Chicago Skyline Debit Card
item.description: Skyline cardholders can use theirs until expiration, but Chase won't be issuing new ones, the bank said.
